i.norm:
Appends a compact, human-readable signature of the given element to {@code summary}, so that the order and shape of streamed elements can be asserted with a single string comparison. The format is: 
tagName[#id][[ownText]][+];
where {@code #id} appears only when the element has an id, {@code [ownText]} only when it has own text, and a trailing {@code +} marks that the element already had a next sibling when it was emitted.
A StreamParser is considered closed once its underlying reader has been released. We reach into the tree builder to read that reader directly, since there is no public flag exposing the closed state.
Fragment parsing exposes the same progressive parse as a full-document stream, just via parseFragment(). The input intentionally omits the first </tr>; the following <tr> infers that closing tag.

Elements are emitted in document order as each one closes, so children precede their parents. A trailing '+' means the element already had a next sibling when it was emitted. Only the fragment is returned (plus the context element at the end of the stack), not a full document.
Once the input is read to completion the parser closes itself and releases its reader.
